key_insight: The paper derives exact closed-form expressions for the expected generalization error in transfer learning for ordinary least squares and under-parameterized linear neural networks, exposing precise bias–variance tradeoffs and conditions under which auxiliary data helps or hurts the main task.
problem_solved: Provides a rigorous theoretical characterization of when and how auxiliary/source data improve (or degrade) generalization on a target/primary task in linear settings—filling gaps in understanding transfer learning benefits and risks.
method: Analytic derivation of exact expected generalization error formulas for ordinary least squares regression.
Bias–variance decomposition to separate the contributions of transfer to systematic error vs. estimation noise.
Extension of the analysis to under-parameterized linear neural networks and identification of alignment/sample-size conditions that control transfer utility.
impact: Gives practitioners actionable criteria to predict whether transfer will help, guiding decisions about using auxiliary datasets, collecting more data, or choosing model capacity. Helps translate theoretical bounds into practical transfer-learning guidelines.
visual_elements: Schematic diagram: source tasks → auxiliary data → transfer → target task, annotated with alignment and sample-size factors.
Stacked bar charts: bias vs. variance components of expected error with and without transfer to show tradeoffs.
Heatmap: expected error improvement as a function of task alignment (similarity) and auxiliary sample size.
Formula callout: compact boxed display of the closed-form expected-error expression with brief annotations of each term (bias term, variance term, alignment factor).
paper_title: Expectation Error Bounds for Transfer Learning in Linear Regression and Linear Neural Networks
paper_authors: Meitong Liu, Christopher Jung, Rui Li, Xue Feng, Han Zhao
